title: CAS History and Recovery
summary: Inspect Git-like history, compare snapshots, and roll back an edge-site incident using SydraDB's immutable metadata model.
whySQLiteFallsShort: SQLite gives you tables and transactions, but not a built-in commit graph with named refs, reflogs, and snapshot diffs over storage metadata.
Rolling metadata back to a known-good commit in SydraDB is a first-class storage workflow instead of an app-specific migration and backup exercise.
Operational history is queryable and reviewable through CAS commands rather than hidden in ad-hoc side tables.

steps.title: Inspect named refs
steps.summary: List the active refs in the edge-east repository and confirm the current head is visible before we compare it to a captured baseline commit.

assertions.message: Expected at least heads/main to be visible.

steps.title: Read commit history
steps.summary: Show the CAS log for heads/main so the incident and rollback context are visible as commit history, not side notes.

assertions.message: Expected more than one commit after baseline plus incident ingestion.

steps.title: Compare checkpoint to current head
steps.summary: Diff the pre-incident baseline commit against heads/main to show what changed before any recovery action is taken.

assertions.message: Incident ingestion should create additional segment or WAL history.

steps.title: Roll back main to the checkpoint
steps.summary: Move heads/main back to the captured baseline commit to prove CAS history is operational, not just diagnostic.

steps.title: Verify live data after rollback
steps.summary: Query the series over HTTP after the rollback and confirm the incident points are gone from the active head.

assertions.message: Baseline points should still be queryable after rollback.
The active head should stop at the baseline point after rollback.

steps.title: Inspect reflog protection
steps.summary: Show the reflog so the rollback event itself is preserved as part of repository history.
